name: Foam rolling
pattern: Self-massage: body weight presses one muscle onto a foam roller or ball while you roll slowly along its length.
setup: Place the roller under the muscle you want to treat, across the muscle's length.
Use hands and feet to set how much body weight goes onto the roller.
Pick a pressure of about 5-7 out of 10: firm, never sharp.

steps.text: Roll slowly along the muscle, about 2-4 seconds from one end to the other.
Roll back the same way. Pause a few breaths on a tender spot if you like.

cues.cue: Slow: 2-4 seconds for each pass along the muscle.
cues.why: Prescriptions with the biggest range-of-motion gains used 2-4 s per roll.
That volume gave the largest range gains; short bouts of 5-10 s already help a little.

cues.cue: Use it in your warm-up or after training for soreness.
cues.why: Before exercise it gives small gains in flexibility and sprint; after, it slightly reduces soreness.

cues.cue: Firm but bearable; breathe and let the muscle soften.
cues.why: Effects are mostly from nervous-system and pain changes, not from breaking up fascia, so more pain is not better.

cues.cue: Keep your trunk braced and roll the muscle, not the joint or bone.
cues.why: Bony points and joints get pressure with no benefit.

breathing: Slow, easy breaths; breathe out as you sink into a tender spot.

tempo.note: 2-4 s per pass, 30-120 s per muscle. Speed itself matters little: slow and fast rolling lowered stiffness about equally.

mistakes.name: Rolling too fast
mistakes.looks: Quick back-and-forth sawing over the roller.
mistakes.fix: Slow down to about 3 seconds per pass.
mistakes.why: Fast passes make it hard to relax and to control pressure; the best-studied dose is 2-4 s per roll.

mistakes.name: Low back sags or arches
mistakes.looks: On the upper back the hips drop and the low back arches over the roller.
mistakes.fix: Lift the hips, brace, hands behind the head.
mistakes.why: Rolls the lumbar spine instead of the muscle.

mistakes.name: Rolling over joints or bone
mistakes.looks: The roller runs over the knee, the shin bone, or the spine's bony points.
mistakes.fix: Stop a hand's width short of the joint.
mistakes.why: Pressure on bone and joints gives no benefit and can bruise.

safety: Skip areas with bruises, open wounds, varicose veins, recent fractures or swelling.
Do not roll the front of the neck or press hard into the belly; use a soft ball and light pressure on the abdomen.
Blood clot history, blood thinners or osteoporosis: ask your doctor first.
Sharp, burning or tingling pain means stop.

variants.change: Ball: smaller, more focused pressure; roll small circles rather than long passes.
Bar or stick roller: you press it on with your hands; same speed and time.
One leg on the roller, the other crossed over: more pressure.

subtypes.name: Neck and upper trapezius
subtypes.change: Lying face up with a soft ball or roller under the back of the neck; small nods and turns, light pressure only.

subtypes.name: Abdomen and hip flexors (ball)
subtypes.change: Face down with a soft ball under the belly or front of the hip; slow breaths, gentle pressure, tiny movements.

subtypes.name: Lats and side of the back
subtypes.change: Side lying, roller under the armpit, bottom arm overhead; roll from the armpit to the bottom of the ribs.

subtypes.name: Chest and front shoulder
subtypes.change: Face down with a ball under the chest just below the collarbone, or lying lengthwise on a roller with arms open; small strokes toward the shoulder.

subtypes.name: Back of the shoulder
subtypes.change: Lying face up, ball under the shoulder blade or back of the shoulder; reach the arm across the body and back.

subtypes.name: Forearms, biceps, triceps
subtypes.change: Arm on the roller or ball on a table or wall; roll from wrist to elbow (forearm) or elbow to shoulder (upper arm).

subtypes.name: Lower back (ball, gentle)
subtypes.change: Use a ball beside (not on) the spine, or a roller only on the muscles to the side; small slow movements. Do not lie with a roller across the lower back.

subtypes.name: Upper back and thoracic
subtypes.match: upper back|thoracic|middle back|rhomboids|trapezius lower|around the world|back stretch|back rotation|kneeling upper back
subtypes.change: Roller across the mid back, hands behind the head, hips lifted; roll from the bottom of the shoulder blades to the top. Thoracic extension: hips down, arch gently over the roller.

subtypes.name: Glutes, piriformis, TFL
subtypes.change: Sit on the roller, cross one ankle over the other knee and lean onto that buttock; roll small passes. TFL: face down and turned slightly, roller at the front-side of the hip.

subtypes.name: Inner thigh
subtypes.change: Face down on the forearms, one knee out to the side with the inner thigh on the roller; roll from near the knee toward the groin.

subtypes.name: Hamstrings
subtypes.change: Sit with the roller under the back of the thighs, hands behind you, hips lifted; roll from the sit bones to just above the knee.

subtypes.name: Quads and outer thigh
subtypes.change: Face down on the forearms in a plank, roller under the front of the thighs; roll from the hip to just above the knee. Turn a little to reach the outer thigh.

subtypes.name: Calves, shins, peroneals, foot
subtypes.change: Calf: sit with the roller under the calves, hands behind, hips lifted; roll from the ankle to below the knee. Shin and peroneals: kneel or side-lie with the roller beside, not on, the shin bone. Foot: stand and roll a ball under the arch.

motion.basis: Default keyframes: upper-back rolling. Dose (2-4 s per pass, 30-120 s per set, 1-3 sets) from behm2020; speed effects from wilke2019 and sezik2024; 5-10 s effects from sullivan2013; up to 2 min on the hamstrings gave no range gain in couture2015. Body angles are estimates of the usual positions; the roller position along the muscle is shown by moving the body with the legs or arms. Subtypes are listed most specific first; the first match wins.
